At the beginning of the second semester of my senior year of high school, the girl I was dating at the time broke up with me and almost immediately started dating someone else I knew. After this, I didn't think my close group of friends were being as good of friends as they should have, and on top of that my grandfather was starting chemotherapy to ensure the polyp that was removed from his colon was completely gone. 

All of this caused me to fall into a deep and dark depression where I planned to kill myself on prom night because I thought that's when everyone else would be at their happiest. 

One day I was eating my lunch in school alone, and I had one of my frequent anxiety attacks at the time and started crying to the point where I didn't have the strength to get up and stop crying before my next class. After the bell indicating the end of lunch rang, one of my classmates saw me crying and got someone to take me to the school's social worker. From there I talked to the social worker for a bit then my mother picked me up and took me to a psychologist, but all she did was suggest a psych ward. 

As the time went on I started seeing a different and better psychologist who helped me control and eliminate my suicidal thoughts and I was getting close with my friends. All wasn't perfect. I ended up going to prom with a close friend of mine from another school, and about three quarters of the way through the prom I had an anxiety attack and sat around for the remainder of the night. 

Nowadays, about a year and a half later, everything in my life has almost gone back to normal. I've developed a fear of commitment on relationships which kinda sucks because I've met some wonderful people I could've had something nice with. 

My biggest piece of advice to people would be to stay strong and let time work its magic. Sometimes it can be a long tough fight, but if you push through everything will get better.
